books.section: Topic 4.9 The Development of an American Culture, B. European Romanticism and American Culture

stimulus.text: Thomas Cole's The Oxbow (View from Mount Holyoke, Northampton, Massachusetts, after a Thunderstorm), painted in 1836, looks down from a high, storm-darkened hillside. On the left, a gnarled tree leans over wild forest under black clouds. On the right, the Connecticut River bends through sunny, cleared farmland dotted with fields and small boats. A tiny figure with an easel stands on the rocks at lower right.
stimulus.source_note: Painting: Thomas Cole, The Oxbow, 1836 (Metropolitan Museum of Art). Public domain; image viewed before writing. Description records only what the painting visibly shows.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: The Oxbow is most closely associated with which of the following?

options.misconception: Both are named American art schools, so it is easy to pick the familiar-sounding one.
Both are famous American art movements, so it is easy to pick the better-known name.
Early American painting means portraits to many students, so it is easy to answer with portraits.

rationales.A: Cole founded the Hudson River School, and The Oxbow is one of its best-known landscapes.
rationales.B: The Ashcan School painted city streets a century later, not wilderness in the 1830s.
rationales.C: Abstract expressionism belongs to the twentieth century, long after Cole's death.
rationales.D: Federalist-era painters made portraits of leaders; Cole painted vast landscapes instead.
rationales.general:
1. Name the painter. The stimulus names Thomas Cole and the year 1836.
2. Match the painter to his school. Cole founded the Hudson River School of American landscape painting.
Background: the school flourished from the 1820s to the 1870s, painting the wild American wilderness.
Remember: link the work to its maker first, then link the maker to the movement.

figures.caption: Thomas Cole, The Oxbow, 1836. Stormy wilderness at left, sunny farmland at right.
figures.alt: Thomas Cole's 1836 painting The Oxbow: a storm-darkened wooded hillside at left, the Connecticut River bending through sunny farmland at right, a tiny artist with an easel on the rocks below
